subject: Duplicate token pseudonymization causing billing surge - evidence & invoice hold request
messages:
From: Emma Linde <emma@pseudosoft.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: payments@pseudosoft.com
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 09:12:00 +01:00
Subject: Sudden token surge after pseudonymization change — can we hold invoice?

Hi Karthik,

We pushed a privacy change on our ingest pipeline on Mar 11 (pseudonymization of user identifiers) and noticed a 3x jump in billed tokens on the next day’s invoice snapshot. Our internal telemetry shows identical request counts but per-request token counts increased dramatically.

We think the upstream change affected input formatting (extra delimiters) and caused tokenization expansion. We need Redwood to:
- Provide per-request token counts (sample) for 2027-03-10 to 2027-03-12
- Put the Mar invoice for Pseudosoft on hold while we and Redwood investigate
- Confirm how any retro credits would be treated for EU VAT (reverse-charge vs. refunded VAT) — Pseudosoft is an EU B2B with VAT ID.

I attached a small sample export (see attachment) and a short mapping of our rollout window. We’re submitting a formal support ticket but wanted to loop you directly since this will impact our March close.

Attachments: [Attachment: sample-requests-20270312.json (JSON, 28KB)]

Thanks,
Emma Linde
Head of Platform
Pseudosoft Ltd
emma@pseudosoft.com

--
On Fri, Mar 12, 2027 at 09:35, Emma Linde <emma@pseudosoft.com> wrote:
> P.S. payments@pseudosoft.com is on CC for collection-hold visibility.
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Emma Linde <emma@pseudosoft.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 10:02:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Sudden token surge after pseudonymization change — can we hold invoice?

Thanks for the heads up, Emma — and sorry you’re seeing this. I’ve escalated to Billing (cc’d) and Engineering to start a tokenization/ingest correlation check. Quick notes and requests so we can move fast:

1) Could you attach a 24–48 hour compressed per-request sample export with request IDs and timestamps (if available) — that will let us map to our per-request logs. The sample-requests file you attached is helpful; if you can add request IDs we’ll crosswalk immediately.

2) I’ve asked Billing to provisionally place a hold on the March invoice for Pseudosoft while we validate. Ben — can you confirm the hold process and whether we need an official request form signed by Pseudosoft payments?

3) On VAT: we’ll have Finance confirm how a retroactive credit would be handled for EU B2B customers (reverse-charge vs refund of VAT). Kimberly — can you loop in tax?

My team expects an initial root-cause signal within 48 hours once we have the request-id export. If it’s a tokenization/mapping issue on our side we’ll propose a provisional credit and the mechanism for VAT handling.

If you prefer, I can open a dedicated shared Drive folder and a short SOC-style evidence checklist to speed the audit.

Karthik
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

[On Mar 12 10:02, in-thread quick reply]
> Karthik: We’ll follow up with the export shortly. Thanks for the rapid pickup.
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Emma Linde <emma@pseudosoft.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 13 Mar 2027 09:15:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Sudden token surge after pseudonymization change — can we hold invoice?

Hi Emma — I’m Ben from Billing; thanks for flagging this and for attaching the sample. To make this audit and provisional action concrete, please can you provide the following as soon as possible: 

• Full per-request token export for 2027-03-09 through 2027-03-13 in CSV (request_id, timestamp, model, tokens_in, tokens_out).
• A brief note about the pseudonymization rollout window and whether any payload transforms (e.g., added separators, base64 wrappers) were applied.
• Confirmation you want the March invoice held pending investigation (we’ll mark as "under review" in our collections system).

What we can do immediately:
• Place a provisional invoice hold if Pseudosoft requests it (we will not send final collection notices while hold is active).
• Run a 72-hour forensic that crosswalks your request_ids with our per-request logs (requires your per-request export).
• If the overcount is attributable to a Redwood-side tokenization/SDK change, propose a provisional credit (we typically estimate a provisional credit up to 20% for first-pass remediation pending full audit).

VAT note: provisional credits are applied to the invoice; tax treatment depends on whether VAT was remitted to tax authorities. Kimberly will advise on EU reverse-charge vs cash refund mechanics.

Attachments: [Attachment: provisional-credit-terms.pdf (PDF, 6KB)]

If you authorize the hold now, we’ll update the account status and pause automated collection emails. Please reply with “Hold invoice” and attach the export.

Ben Carter
Billing Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

[internal] Kimberly — FYI on tax mechanism; Pseudosoft reports EU VAT ID on their billing profile.
From: Emma Linde <emma@pseudosoft.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: payments@pseudosoft.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 15:04:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Sudden token surge after pseudonymization change — can we hold invoice?

Ben / Karthik — attaching the per-request export you requested and a short rollout note. We confirm: please place the March invoice on hold while investigation is open.

Attachments:
- usage-export-20270312.csv (CSV, 1.2MB) — per-request tokens with request_id
- sample-requests-20270312.json (already attached)

On VAT: Pseudosoft is EU B2B (VAT ID: EU123456789). We expect reverse-charge treatment for any retroactive credit, but will coordinate with Kimberly’s team if documentation is required. Can you please provide a point of contact in Redwood’s Tax/Finance team?

We appreciate the quick turnaround. Please confirm the account status change and the expected timeline for the forensic audit.

Thanks,
Emma
Head of Platform
Pseudosoft Ltd
emma@pseudosoft.com
